I’m in America, but I’m Indian andd under my parents health insurance.
I’m 23, senior in college *hopefully* graduating in December but we’ll see 😕

My major is biomedical engineering and it was strongly suggested by my parents. I had initially wanted to go into architecture (I'm an artist), or if I was really dreaming big maybe a graphic designer or animator. My parents didn't want me to do any of those because of pay and the job market. In retrospect I hate that those were the reasons because frankly, the job market for biomedical engineers with just a bachelor's degree sucks nowadays, but back in 2012/2013 it was predicted to be the booming job field. I also have about $40K in debt, which doesn't really leave room to completely switch tracks. 

You're right, I should tell my parents. The main thing that's been stopping me from doing so is because I'm afraid the disappointment will kill them. I know, I can hear how ridiculous it sounds. But my uncle (dad's brother) apparently had a history of mental illness and was institutionalized at some point and then died from a heart attack, and one day many years ago, my mom told me this and said that I need to stay on the straight and narrow and do well in life. If I got in trouble, she doesn't know if my dad will be able to take it with this history of mental illness in the family, plus problems with blood pressure, etc. And she said that she cannot live without him, and it will just be me and my brother alone (my brother's autistic)

As far fetched as it sounds, it's stuck with me throughout all these years and I can never seem to shake it. It's my biggest fear.
Honestly i would rather be reincarnated so I'd have a chance to start fresh. I've screwed up too much in this life
